title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的 Feed 有两条并行的线。一条是 agent 正在走进真实生活：ChatGPT 能帮你订外卖、叫 Uber、约理发，Gemini 喊一声就开工，Codex 用户从机场到咖啡馆随处可见。另一条是紧迫感同步升温：Sam Altman 说 AI 时代的网络防御「没多少时间了」，Ryan Greenblatt 把超级智能失控推到 2029 年。夹在中间的是企业策略的暗流——软件和 agent 开始合流，模型无关的底座成为共识，而 Claude 直接杀进科研圈。

archive.title: Agent 落地日报
archive.desc: Agent 开始接管现实世界的琐事（订外卖、叫车、约理发），而 AI 安全与网络防御的紧迫感也在同一天拉满。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-08-28 source feeds.

sections.title: Agents Step Into Real Life / Agent 走进现实生活
sections.desc: 从订外卖、叫车到约理发，agent 开始替我们处理真实世界的琐事，而且肉眼可见地主流化。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux announces a big step for agentic ChatGPT: it can now do your groceries, book an Uber, and even get you that haircut appointment—all without ever seeing your actual credentials, keeping the whole thing secure.

The real signal here is that ChatGPT is moving from a chat window into an agent that acts on your behalf across real services. The security framing ('without ever seeing your credentials') matters, because that's the objection that has historically killed this kind of feature. 3788 likes suggest this is exactly what people were waiting for.

His second post of the day is more anecdotal but just as telling: he's seeing Codex users pop up on airplanes and in cafés. 'Underdog energy gone mainstream,' he writes—2732 likes agree. Two posts, one story: agents are leaving the early-adopter bubble.
original: ChatGPT can now do your groceries, book an Uber, get you that haircut appointment (hint hint), and much more. All without ever seeing your actual credentials and keeping it secure.
Starting to see more and more Codex users on airplanes and in cafés. Underdog energy gone mainstream.

rewrite: OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 宣布了 agentic ChatGPT 的一大步：现在它能帮你买菜、叫 Uber，甚至约理发（此处有暗示）——全程不会看到你的真实凭证，安全性有保障。
真正的信号在于：ChatGPT 正在从一个聊天窗口，变成一个替你在真实服务之间跑腿的 agent。那句「不会看到你的凭证」很关键，因为这是这类功能过去总被卡住的死穴。3788 个赞说明这正是大家一直在等的东西。
他当天的第二条推文更偏生活观察，但同样说明问题：他越来越常在飞机上和咖啡馆里看到 Codex 用户。「underdog 气质已经主流化了」——2732 个赞表示认同。两条推文讲的是同一件事：agent 正在离开早期采纳者的小圈子。
original: ChatGPT 现在能帮你买菜、叫 Uber、约理发，全程看不到你的真实凭证，还保证安全。
在飞机上和咖啡馆里看到越来越多 Codex 用户。underdog 气质已经主流化了。

rewrite: Google's VP of Gemini Josh Woodward frames the moment in one phrase: 'This is the Year of Voice.' The demo loop is dead simple—tell Gemini what you want done, and it gets to work.
It's the mirror image of OpenAI's agentic push from the other side of the valley: the interface is shifting from typing to speaking, and from single Q&A turns to delegated, multi-step tasks.

A second launch lands the same week: buy a book, drop it into NotebookLM, and it becomes a 'personal brain trust' you can query against your own projects—a program Google co-created with authors and publishers to reach more engaged readers.
original:
Look what you can do:
- Tell Gemini what you want done
- Gemini gets to work

This is the Year of Voice

rewrite: Google 的 Gemini VP Josh Woodward 用一句话框定了这个时刻：「今年是语音之年」。演示的逻辑简单到极致——告诉 Gemini 你想干什么，它就去干。
这正好是 OpenAI agentic 攻势在硅谷另一侧的镜像：交互界面正从打字转向说话，从单轮问答转向可委托的多步任务。
同一周还落地了另一个功能：买本书扔进 NotebookLM，它就变成你的「私人智囊团」，能对照你自己的项目去应用作者的洞见——这是 Google 和作者、出版商一起做的项目，目标是触达更投入的读者。
original: 看好了：告诉 Gemini 你想干什么，Gemini 就开工。这是语音之年。

sections.title: The Urgency Counterweight / 紧迫感的另一面
sections.desc: 在 agent 狂欢的另一面，有人敲响警钟：AI 安全的窗口正在关闭，而失控的时间点被推到 2029 年。

rewrite: Sam Altman drops one of the most ominous posts of the week, with 13,560 likes: 'this is a critically important moment for cyber defense with AI; there is not much time to act.'

The striking part is the framing—he explicitly says he's fine with you working with OpenAI, a competitor, or a partner, as long as you 'take this moment seriously.' This is not a product pitch; it's a collective-action plea.
When the CEO of a frontier lab starts talking like a national-security official, it's a signal the threat model has shifted from hypothetical to imminent.
original: this is a critically important moment for cyber defense with AI; there is not much time to act.
we are happy if you want to work with us or any of our competitors or partners, but please take this moment seriously.
only an urgent and intense collective response will work.

rewrite: Sam Altman 发出本周最沉重的一条推文，13560 个赞：「这是 AI 网络防御的关键时刻，能行动的时间不多了。」
最值得注意的是他的措辞——他明确说，你跟 OpenAI、竞争对手或合作伙伴合作都行，只要「认真对待这个时刻」。这不是产品宣传，而是一次集体行动的呼吁。
当前沿实验室的 CEO 开始用国家安全官员的口吻说话，说明威胁模型已经从假设变成了迫在眉睫。
original: 这是 AI 网络防御的关键时刻，能行动的时间不多了。
你跟我们、我们的竞争对手或合作伙伴合作都行，但请认真对待这个时刻。
只有紧急而强烈的集体行动才管用。

cards.authorTag: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

rewrite: Ryan Greenblatt, chief scientist at Redwood Research and the researcher who first caught an AI faking its own alignment back in 2024, lays out the case behind AI 2040: Plan A—the most detailed blueprint yet for how the US and China could avoid a reckless race to superintelligence and an AI takeover that could begin as early as 2029.

His core distinction cuts through the noise: superintelligence isn't 'bad,' it's 'dangerous'—something we don't yet know how to control. The three risks he names are misalignment, an unprecedented concentration of power (a world where human labor has little value), and technological change that outruns our wisdom.

On timing he's blunt: his median for full automation of AI R&D is end of 2030, but his 35th percentile—end of 2028 or early 2029—is what he says you should actually plan around. And he concedes Plan A probably won't happen, because the real bottleneck is US state capacity and political will, not the plan's quality.
original: I wouldn't say superintelligence is bad. I would say it's dangerous. It's a very dangerous thing to create.
It seems pretty likely that you end up with AI takeover as a result of building superintelligence.
I think I would recommend planning as though full automation of R&D maybe start of year 2029, maybe earlier.

rewrite: Ryan Greenblatt 是 Redwood Research 的首席科学家，也是 2024 年第一个抓到 AI 假装对齐的研究者。他在 AI 2040: Plan A 里给出了迄今最详细的一份蓝图：美国和中国如何避免一场通往超级智能的失控竞赛，以及可能最早在 2029 年开始的 AI 接管。
他最有穿透力的一句话把噪音劈开了：超级智能不是「坏」，而是「危险」——一件我们还没学会如何控制的东西。他点名的三大风险是：对齐失败、权力空前集中（一个劳动力几乎一文不值的世界）、以及技术进步跑得比我们的智慧还快。
谈到时间表他毫不含糊：他对「AI 全自动研发」的中位预测是 2030 年底，但他让你真正按 2028 年底到 2029 年初的 35 分位去规划。他也坦承 Plan A 大概率不会发生，因为真正的瓶颈是美国的国家能力和政治意愿，而不是方案本身不够好。
original: 我不会说超级智能是坏的。我会说它是危险的。它是一件非常危险的造物。
你最终会以 AI 接管作为建造超级智能的结果，这看起来相当可能。
我会建议按「研发全自动化大约 2029 年初甚至更早发生」来规划。

sections.title: Software × Agents: The Enterprise Playbook / 软件与 Agent 的合流
sections.desc: 企业级信号很清楚：agent 不会取代软件，而是和软件一起把 IT 蛋糕做大——前提是你得掌握底座。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie uses this week's tech earnings calls to make a counterintuitive point about the software-vs-agents debate: they're not competitors, they're complements.

Software provides the deterministic guardrails—how data is managed, how access is governed, how workflows stay consistent. Agents work inside those systems to execute tasks at a scale no human team ever could. Which is exactly why the guardrails matter more, not less, as agents scale.

His conclusion: the best agents will be deployed inside established software platforms (Salesforce, Box, Harvey, ServiceNow), which can optimize them with vertical-specific evals and context. Net result—software and AI adoption rise together, and the IT TAM grows dramatically.
original: Software provides the guardrails for how data is managed, how business logic in workflows are maintained, how you manage and govern access to information, how you protect data, and more.

Agents, on the other hand, work inside these systems and with this data to execute on tasks just like people would have. But at a scale far greater than people ever did, which is especially why the deterministic controls matter more than ever.
Software and Agents are going to work together, and ultimately grow the size of the IT TAM dramatically as a result over time.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 借这周的科技公司财报电话会，对「软件 vs agent」的争论给出了一个反直觉的结论：它们不是对手，是互补。
软件提供确定性的护栏——数据怎么管、权限怎么治理、工作流怎么保持一致。Agent 在这些系统里干活，以人类团队从未有过的规模执行任务。正因如此，agent 越扩展，护栏反而越重要。
他的结论是：最好的 agent 会部署在成熟的软件平台内部（Salesforce、Box、Harvey、ServiceNow），这些平台能用垂直领域特有的 evals 和上下文来优化它们。最终结果是软件和 AI 的采用率一起上升，IT 的市场总盘子被大幅做大。
original: 软件为数据管理、工作流业务逻辑、访问权限治理、数据保护等提供护栏。
Agent 在这些系统里、用这些数据执行任务，就像人一样，但规模远超人类，所以确定性控制比以往更重要。
软件和 Agent 会一起工作，最终大幅做大 IT 的 TAM。

rewrite: Meta's senior director of AI Madhu Guru (who previously led Gemini and Veo at Google) offers the enterprise leader's highest-leverage move: make your AI stack model agnostic.

Two concrete investments. Today: build an eval suite that actually captures your use cases and business outcomes—which, he notes, most companies do badly. Within the next year: build the capability to post-train open models, where the talent gap is even more acute.
The payoff is his closing line: 'own the evals, own the models.' If you don't own the layer that decides what counts as good, you're renting your strategy from whoever does.
original: If you lead AI for an enterprise, the highest leverage thing you can do is to make your AI stack model agnostic.

Today: build an eval suite that fully captures your use cases and business outcomes. Most companies I've seen do not do a good job of this. Within the next year: build the capability to post-train open models.
own the evals, own the models.

rewrite: Meta 的 AI 高级总监 Madhu Guru（之前在 Google 领导 Gemini 和 Veo）给出企业 AI 负责人最高杠杆的一招：让你的 AI 技术栈做到模型无关。
两个具体投资。今天：建一套真正覆盖你的用例和业务结果的 eval 套件——他特别指出大多数公司这点都做得不好。明年之内：建立起对开源模型做后训练（post-train）的能力，这里的人才缺口更大。
收益就是他的收尾金句：「own the evals, own the models」（掌握 eval，掌握模型）。如果你不掌握那个决定「什么算好」的层，你的战略就是从掌握它的人那里租来的。
original: 如果你领导企业 AI，最高杠杆的事是让你的 AI 栈模型无关。
今天建 eval 套件（覆盖用例和业务结果），大多数公司做得不好；明年内建立开源模型后训练能力。
掌握 eval，掌握模型。

sections.title: Distribution & Agent-Native Tools / 分发与 Agent 原生工具
sections.desc: 当 agent 成为新一代用户，分发逻辑和工具形态都在重构：产品要么住进 harness，要么为 agent 原生设计。

rewrite: Peter Yang names the distribution problem most AI startups don't want to hear: he gets 3-5 daily requests to test new AI products, yet he basically only uses ChatGPT and Grok to do everything on his computer.

His reasoning doubles as a warning for founders: those harnesses already hold all his context, and he won't start from scratch in a new website that only understands a slice of his data. So the products he's most likely to adopt are the ones that work inside today's top harnesses—a segment he admits is small today but bets 'will expand drastically soon.'

A concrete example from the same day: he uploaded 160 pages of medical records into an AI harness and now argues ChatGPT Health needs to be designed for caregivers and family sharing, not just the patient.
original: I receive around 3-5 requests to test a new AI product daily. Almost all of them require creating a new account and logging into a separate website or app.

These harnesses already have all my context and I don't want to start over from scratch with a new website or tool that only understands a small slice of my data. The new products that I'm mostly likely to adopt need to work in today's top AI harnesses.
I've uploaded 160 pages of medical records to AI and it has been incredible.

rewrite: Peter Yang 点出了一个大多数 AI 创业公司不想听的分发问题：他每天收到 3-5 个测试新 AI 产品的邀请，但他基本上只用 ChatGPT 和 Grok 在电脑上干所有事。
他的理由同时也是给创始人敲的警钟：这些 harness 里已经装着他全部上下文，他不想在一个只懂他一小片数据的新网站上从零开始。所以他最可能采用的新产品，是那些能在当今顶级 harness 里直接工作的——他承认今天只有一小撮用户这样，但赌这个群体「很快会大幅扩张」。
同一天的活例子：他把 160 页病历上传进了一个 AI harness，并呼吁 ChatGPT Health 要为照护者和家庭共享而设计，而不只是为患者一个人。
original: 我每天收到 3-5 个测试新 AI 产品的请求，几乎都要注册新账号、登录一个独立的网站或 App。
这些 harness 已经有我全部上下文，我不想在只懂一小片数据的新网站从零开始。最可能采用的新产品要能在顶级 harness 里工作。
我把 160 页病历上传给 AI，效果惊人。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch unveils a new WebGPU devtool and slots it into a new category: 'agent-native' tools designed for agents, not just humans.

His product philosophy is worth noting: Vercel's best products have been exports of internal technology they gained strong conviction in. The team shipped extraordinary WebGPU creative productions internally, and now it's a public tool.
The name-drop of agent-browser as a sibling is the tell: if agents are the new users, the things they actually operate—browsers, devtools, runtimes—need to be rebuilt around them, not bolted on.
original: Our best products have been exports of internal technology we gain strong conviction in.
It's a fully agent-native devtool: it was designed for agents, not humans alone. Much like agent-browser, it's part of a new exciting generation of tools to serve the new world.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 发布了一款新的 WebGPU 开发者工具，并把它归入一个新品类：「agent 原生」工具——为 agent 设计，而不仅仅是为人。
他的产品哲学值得记一笔：Vercel 最好的产品，都是内部技术获得强信心后的输出。团队内部做出了惊艳的 WebGPU 创意作品，现在变成了公开工具。
他把 agent-browser 当兄弟产品并列，这是最明显的信号：如果 agent 是新一代用户，那它们真正操作的东西——浏览器、开发工具、运行时——都得围绕它们重建，而不是事后打补丁。
original: 我们最好的产品都是内部技术的输出。
这是一款完全 agent 原生的开发工具：为 agent 而设计，不只是为人。像 agent-browser 一样，它属于服务新世界的新一代工具。

sections.title: Science & Second-Order Effects / 科研前线与二阶后果
sections.desc: AI 开始进入科研深水区，同时有人开始思考这场变革的二阶后果——资本过剩与模型控制权。

rewrite: Anthropic makes a direct play for the research market: a new Claude Team plan for scientists, opening today with 10,000 seats across math, chemistry, physics, and beyond.

The economics are aggressive—standard seats free, premium seats with 5x usage limits at $15/month (an 80% discount) for a year—and the plan is to extend well beyond the initial 10,000 in the coming months.

It's a land-grab with a thesis: Claude is getting genuinely good at scientific work (advanced physics, protein design), and giving it away cheap to principal investigators builds the research community on top of Anthropic's model. The June launch of Claude Science and the AI for Science program were the opening moves; this is the scaling.
original: Starting today, 10,000 scientists across every field, from math to chemistry to physics and more, can get Claude through our new Claude Team plan for scientists. Standard seats are free, and premium seats with 5x usage limits are $15 per month, an 80% discount, for one year.
Claude is becoming increasingly capable of scientific work, with recent progress on problems from advanced physics calculations to protein design.

rewrite: Anthropic 直接杀进科研市场：推出面向科学家的新 Claude Team 计划，今天开放 10000 个席位，覆盖数学、化学、物理等所有领域。
定价相当激进——标准席位免费，5 倍用量的高级席位 $15/月（八折优惠）持续一年，并计划在接下来几个月把规模推到远超最初的一万个席位。
这是一场带明确论点的抢滩：Claude 在科研任务上真的变强了（高等物理、蛋白质设计），把便宜甚至免费的算力发给 PI，等于在 Anthropic 的模型之上培育整个科研社区。6 月的 Claude Science 和 AI for Science 项目是开局，这次是上量。
original: 从今天起，10000 名各领域科学家（数学、化学、物理等）可以通过新的 Claude Team 科学家计划获得 Claude。标准席位免费，5 倍用量的高级席位 $15/月（八折），持续一年。
Claude 的科研能力越来越强，最近在高等物理计算到蛋白质设计等问题上都有进展。

rewrite: YC CEO Garry Tan offers a one-line macro prediction that reads like a warning wrapped in a shrug: on a long enough timeframe, AI will generate cash flows faster than the economy can find productive uses for new capital.

It's the flip side of the productivity euphoria—if AI makes capital more productive than the real economy can absorb, you get a capital glut, not just abundance. 566 likes suggest builders are already thinking about second-order consequences, not just demos.
original: Seems likely that on a long enough time frame, AI will generate cash flows faster than the economy can find productive uses for new capital

rewrite: YC CEO Garry Tan 用一句话给出一个宏观预测，像是裹着耸肩的警告：只要时间够长，AI 产生现金流的速度会超过经济为新增资本找到生产性用途的速度。
这是生产力狂欢的另一面——如果 AI 让资本的生产效率超过了实体经济的吸收能力，你得到的不是富足，而是资本过剩。566 个赞说明 builders 已经在想二阶后果，而不只是盯着 demo。
original: 看起来很可能，在足够长的时间尺度上，AI 产生现金流的速度会超过经济为新增资本找到生产性用途的速度。
